answer: Each agent must continuously refresh a unique pigment bond drawn from scarce local entropy. To collect rewards the bond must bridge a randomized karst of multi-hop attestation paths; every hop irreversibly burns a fixed fraction of the pigment. Creating N sybil identities therefore requires N independent entropy sources and pays linear, non-amortizable burn costs that scale directly with the number of fakes, while one honest agent recycles a single pigment.
